chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'No one pauses upon those mountains, neither a righteous one nor an immoral one, except that Allah answers for him. As for the righteous one, he is answered in his Hereafter and his world; and as for the immoral one, he is answered in his world.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in the answer to supplication for the righteous versus the immoral at the mountains of Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni, highlights the spiritual potency of specific mountainous sites during Hajj, where divine response is guaranteed for all supplicants. It offers a nuanced theological distinction: the righteous (al-barr) receive a comprehensive reward encompassing both worldly benefits and eternal salvation, whereas the immoral (al-fajir) receive their portion of the answer primarily in this world, often as a 'consumption' of their reward before the Hereafter.
